intervals.label: ALPHA-g (2021 – present)
intervals.note: Official site hardware list; end is the 31 August 2026 start of Long Shutdown 3.

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 3 (no antiproton beam)
intervals.note: The Antimatter Factory (AD and ELENA) delivered its last beams on 31 August 2026 and "will progressively return to operation from 2028 onwards, with the different injectors and facilities restarting in stages" (CERN, 31 August 2026); no experiment-specific restart date is published, so the end is left open.
intervals.quote: CERN’s injector complex and Antimatter Factory took their final steps towards Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) this morning, as the last particle beams were extracted and the machines fell silent.

name: ALPHA-g
notes: Hall for ALPHA-g is an assumption flagged on the placement: the official page lists the apparatus but not its hall.

placements.note: Hall placement inferred from "an experiment based at CERN's AD hall"; the official page does not name the hall for ALPHA-g; campus-grade site used.

summary.plain: The vertical trap of the ALPHA experiment. Antihydrogen atoms are released from a magnetic trap and the detectors record whether they fall or rise, a direct test of how antimatter responds to gravity.
summary.technical: ALPHA-g: vertical double Penning-Malmberg and neutral-atom trap, about twice the size of ALPHA 2/3, built to measure the gravitational acceleration of antihydrogen released from magnetic confinement; operating since 2021.

technology.quote: New vertical system of about double the size of ALPHA 2/3. Double Penning-Malmber trap and neutral atom traps.
technology.value: Vertical Penning-Malmberg and neutral-atom trap system, about double the size of ALPHA 2/3, with a precisely built, low-persistent-current magnet set
